A touchdown betting tip I’ve used for years: research the game before picking the scorer.

Don’t build a TD parlay by grabbing one name from every matchup just to fill the slip.

Start with higher game totals, then check each team’s implied points, defensive vulnerabilities, and who actually gets the goal-line carries and red-zone targets.

Sometimes two players from one favorable matchup deserve a closer look than forcing picks across five different games. But sharing a high-total game doesn’t automatically make them a good pairing…or a good bet at the odds offered.

A high total gets my attention. The player’s role and price decide whether I bet.

Jaylen Waddle

Waddle gets a theoretically softer matchup against Arizona, but one I don’t think sets up quite that strongly for him. For starters, this offense is just really bad right now, and the connection between Waddle and Nix has not appeared too strong to start. Waddle is just 66th of 89 WRs in catchable target rate this year (75% of targets), despite a relatively low 9.3 aDOT. Of WRs with a sub-10 yard aDOT, no WR sits at a lower catchable target rate, per @FantasyPtsData.

The Cardinals also have shown the most strength defending the slot this year, as they’re allowing the 10th fewest YPG there (despite 10th most pass YPG overall). Waddle ran a ton from the slot in Week 1 before coming down a bit there, but he’s still running roughly 40% of his routes there since Week 1.

The 2-high (ARI leads NFL in 2-high rate at nearly 70%) shells have also historically limited Waddle’s production, and that’s continued to come through in 2026. He dips from 0.24→0.15 TPRR against 2-high (-37.5%!), and 1.49→1.21 YPRR against it. 

Similarly, he’s been worse off against Cover 6, which Arizona runs at a league-high 32.1% rate. Since 2025, he’s dipped from 0.25→0.23 TPRR vs. Cover 6, and 2.15→1.54 YPRR.

I have hope in Waddle longer term this year still, but I think he’s overpriced given what we’ve seen from this offense AND the schematic set-up.

Matthew Golden

Golden is off to an electric start to his sophomore season, 6th in the entire NFL in receiving yards. He’s looking like a stud, separating at a high level (13th in separation market share) and earning elite volume (top 5 among WRs in targets).

In Week 7, Golden gets the premier matchup, against a Detroit pass defense that has been abysmal (29th in EPA/DB). They’ve been vulnerable on the perimeter (29th in YPG allowed, 31st in EPA/target), where Golden runs ~80% of his routes. 

Detroit also runs a lot of man coverage (4th highest rate over last month per @FantasyPtsData), which Golden has been an absolute dog against. He’s 20th among 79 WRs in route win rate against man, while top 6 in both YPRR (3.16) and TPRR (0.38).

The one thing Detroit has been doing relatively well is bringing pressure (6th highest rate). Golden, however, is Love’s go-to under pressure. He easily leads the team with 18 targets when they’re under pressure (nearly double next highest at 10), and is sitting at an impressive 3.90 YPRR and 0.26 TPRR, both marks leading the entire NFL.

I’m expecting the strong start for Golden to continue here, in a potential shootout environment.
